 MAHB to spend RM131mil upgrading 12 STOLports nationwide
 By DIVYA THERESA RAVI  and  RAGANANTHINI VETHASALAM 
 Monday, 16 Nov 2026
 | 12:54 PM MYT

 Sabah & Sarawak 
 28 Aug 2026 
 RM30mil approved to upgrade two airports in rural Sarawak 
 KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB) will undertake RM131mil worth of infrastructure upgrades at 12 short take-off and landing airports (STOLports) nationwide to strengthen safety management and emergency preparedness following the recent helicopter crash in Long Lellang.
 Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said the upgrades will include runway resurfacing, perimeter fencing replacements, the construction of perimeter roads, and terminal building improvements.
 "These works are planned to be implemented in phases starting in 2027 and are expected to be fully completed by December 2028, subject to procurement and project implementation processes," he told the Dewan Rakyat on Monday (Nov 16).
 He was responding to Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar), who asked about the ministry's efforts to improve safety management and emergency response across Sarawak's STOLports in the wake of the incident.
 Beyond physical infrastructure, Hasbi said MAHB is tightening documentation and safety compliance requirements, bolstering rescue and firefighting capabilities, and increasing manpower at STOLports.
 In response to a supplementary question from Shafizan, Hasbi revealed that an estimated RM10.615mil has been earmarked for immediate improvements at the Long Lellang STOLport.
 Scheduled to run from the first quarter of 2027 through the first quarter of 2028, these works will cover the resurfacing of the runway, taxiway, and aircraft parking apron. A specialised Rapid Intervention Vehicle (RIV) for firefighting will also be deployed there, supported by the phased recruitment of 15 additional personnel.
 Addressing the status of the newly opened Bebuling STOLport, Hasbi noted that final operational approval is still pending for aerodrome certification and an Aerodrome Operating Licence from the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM).
 Meanwhile, Shaharizukirnain Abd Kadir (PN-Setiu) asked whether the government would ground helicopters of the same model involved in the Long Lellang crash pending investigation results, and whether flight data and cockpit voice recorders should be made mandatory for medical evacuation helicopters.
 Hasbi replied that there are currently no plans to suspend Flying Doctor Service helicopters, as the fleet has already passed CAAM airworthiness inspections.
 "The investigation is still ongoing, and a final report on this aviation accident must be prepared within one year. All damaged equipment, engines, and related components have already been sent to an overseas laboratory—specifically to the engine manufacturer—for examination.
 "Within a year, we will have specific answers as to why the accident occurred," he said.
